newsitem.title: USA: Ohio Poll shows Clinton widened lead.
newsitem.headline: Ohio Poll shows Clinton widened lead.

text.p: President Clinton has widened his lead over Bob Dole to 13 points in Ohio, a University of Cincinnati tracking poll said Wednesday.

Ohio, with 21 electoral votes, is a key state that has voted on the winning side in all but two presidential contests this century. No Republican has ever been elected president without carrying the state.
Asked by phone who they planned to vote for, 48 percent of likely voters polled said Clinton and 35 percent said Dole, the university said.
In the university's most recent previous tracking polls Clinton's lead was 8 to 9 points.
The latest poll included 566 likely voters interviewed last Thursday through Sunday and had an error margin of plus or minus 4.1 points.
Reform Party candidate Ross Perot gained a point, with 8 percent saying they planned to vote for him. Two percent named other candidates and 6 percent remained undecided, the university said.
The poll was sponsored by the university, the Cincinnati Enquirer newspaper and WLWT television.
